categories.main_business_segments: The company primarily operates in cloud computing services, intelligent computing cloud services (AI computing), and Internet Data Center (IDC) services. It provides computing cloud products such as CPU-based cloud hosts, bare metal servers, storage, and edge computing, as well as GPU-based intelligent computing services for AI model training and inference. IDC services include data center resource leasing, bandwidth, and IP address rental, along with value-added services and self-operated data center construction.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company utilizes virtualization, distributed computing, software-defined networking (SDN), distributed storage, and cloud-native technologies. It has developed proprietary platforms like the GIC platform for global cloud and network resource management and the Cloud OS integrated cloud service platform based on KVM virtualization. The intelligent computing cloud leverages GPU clusters, high-speed interconnects (400G networks), and supports heterogeneous computing and container cloud products.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers are from industries such as internet, gaming, e-commerce, video streaming, online education, and finance. The company serves large and medium-sized enterprises requiring cloud and IDC services, including AI large model enterprises and AIGC application companies. It also targets cross-border e-commerce, internet tools, and digital transformation enterprises.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates globally with business presence in over 50 countries and regions, including China, North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, and Hong Kong, Macau, and Taiwan. It has 24 regional zones, 52 availability zones, 94 data centers, and thousands of edge computing nodes worldwide. Key overseas data centers are located in the United States (Dallas), Singapore, Germany, and others.
categories.supply_chain_position: The company operates primarily as a midstream cloud service provider and IDC operator. It procures infrastructure resources such as cabinets, bandwidth, and IP addresses from upstream telecom operators (China Telecom, China Unicom, China Mobile) and integrates these with its own hardware and software to provide cloud and IDC services downstream to enterprise customers.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include expanding intelligent computing cloud capabilities, deepening cooperation with domestic AI large model customers and chip manufacturers, and enhancing global cloud network integration. R&D focuses on upgrading the integrated cloud platform, elastic bare metal systems, and rendering integrated intelligent computing platforms. The company emphasizes autonomous innovation, cloud-native technologies, heterogeneous computing, and GPU resource optimization.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is generated mainly through pay-as-you-go and subscription models for cloud computing services, including CPU and GPU cloud hosts, bandwidth, and IP address rentals. IDC services generate revenue from leasing data center cabinets and bandwidth, with additional income from value-added services and equipment sales. The company also benefits from procurement and resale price differences of telecom resources.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: The company positions itself as a neutral cloud service provider with a focus on security, flexibility, and efficiency, avoiding competing with its customers. It competes in the cloud computing and IDC sectors against major telecom operators and third-party IDC providers. Its global network integration and proprietary platforms provide competitive advantages in service delivery and customer experience.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2023, the company reported revenues of approximately RMB 1.24 billion, a 1.67% increase from 2022, but incurred a net loss attributable to shareholders of about RMB 340 million, worsening from the previous year. The company has experienced steady revenue growth over four consecutive years but faces profitability challenges due to overseas resource underutilization and asset impairments. Total assets were about RMB 2.08 billion at year-end 2023, with a decline in net assets by 28.16%.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: The company emphasizes its global one-network architecture enabling high-speed, secure, and integrated cloud and network services worldwide. Its proprietary GIC and Cloud OS platforms allow rapid deployment and flexible management of cloud resources. The company highlights its neutral stance ensuring data security and independence for customers, strong R&D capabilities, and tailored solutions for AI large model training and inference, supporting diverse industry digital transformation needs.
